_about.what: Cities, towns and sieges (the grand campaign). The town is the key to its province: an army that wins the country round it has not taken the province until the town itself is stormed or gives in.
_about.room: How many corps the town can hold as its garrison, by the size of the place. Fortress works add fortRoom.
_about.bonus: How much stronger a garrison fights inside the town, by the size of the place. fortBonus is added for each level of fortress works. Bombardment breaks part of it down.
_about.guard: The town's own guard of depot troops, police and militia, in divisions' worth, while the place is held by the country it belongs to. It is never more than guardShare of that country's army, so a small country's capital has a small guard. guardOrg is how steady it is.
_about.startIn: Ruling 232's mend for a city whose record garrison was inside before any field army fell back (the design director's b566 and b567: Warsaw, September 1939). With driveOut on, a 1939 grand campaign opens with each corps named here (a row of setup-1939.json, by nation and name) inside its own town as a garrison, under the record's name, commander and experience: the same divisions, so nothing is counted twice. Warsaw's is the Warsaw Defence Command under Walerian Czuma, the city's own troops, 2 divisions at 0.05 experience with the city's guns and its 33 light tanks folded in. The rest comes by play: a staff or a player may order retreating corps in under 232(d).
_about.driveOut: Ruling 232 (beat the army, take the city): when true, a field army beaten in a province never falls back into its town (not even its own capital): it falls back to open country next door, or lays down its arms if it has no ground of its side to go to and no ship to lift it. Where no garrison stands in the town, its guard fights beside the field army in the same battle, behind its walls, and when the field is won the guard is taken and the town falls with the province in that one order. A garrison ordered in beforehand still holds the town after the field is lost. A test or a run can set it by TC_DRIVE=1 or 0.
_about.rings: Ruling 232's rider b606 (the historian's city-garrisons-b605.md). A startIn row that carries 'town' and 'divs' is no row of the roster: its corps (infantry, held) is raised in that town's province on the first day only where ruling 232 holds, so the history campaign and a war with the ruling off have no such corps. A startIn row may carry 'str', the share of its divisions it stands at from the first day and never fills past (Kiev's Fortified Region: skeleton units, NKVD and the schools, 0.25 of a division, here 2 divisions at an eighth; Helsinki's coast forts, flak and Civil Guard, 0.3), and 'fortress', a mark that keeps it inside when a computer's staff would send a garrison with no enemy near back to the field. Each row of 'rings' is a ring the record manned in the month its country was first attacked: the first time anyone declares war on 'nat', the corps named, if it still stands inside 'town', fills to its full divisions before the attacker's battles that month, with men from the reserve as a call-up wave's are and as far as the reserve allows, at order 'org'. Once. No staff reads it: what goes in after (the 37th Army) is the staff's own.
_about.lateGarrison: Ruling 232, rider b587 (the late garrison; only while driveOut is on): at the history dial's stops named in 'stops', a computer staff with an enemy field army one march from its capital, or from a city of its own whose works stand at ai.great.works or higher, orders into the town, up to its room, the worn corps standing in that province (those that fell back into it among them), the most worn first: a corps under 'str' of its strength or under 'org' of its order. Fresh corps stay in the field. It is an order like any garrison, its month spent; a beaten army's retreat still never goes inside.
_about.stores: Months a town closely invested feeds its defenders before they go hungry. Each level of fortress works adds fortStores. A harbour the defenders' ships can still reach is never starved.
_about.ring: Divisions outside for each division inside before the town is closely invested and its stores run down. Troops of the besieger's side in the provinces next door count too, at ringNear of their weight, and a town with every road out of it in enemy hands is shut in whatever stands at its gates.
_about.summons: A town held only by its guard opens its gates to a force with these odds or better, without a fight. The sizes in summonsNot never do: a city or a capital has to be stormed or starved.
_about.pocket: A part of a country cut off from the rest of it lives on the stores of its biggest town and then goes hungry, depot or no depot. It is cut off when it is fewer than least provinces and less than share of the country's home ground, every road out of it runs into ground an enemy holds, and no ship can reach it from another port of its side. The stores are laid in for the garrison the town has room for: more corps than that eat them faster in proportion. No drafts reach the troops inside. A town's harbour feeds it only while its side has another port to send the ships from.
_about.stand: A country whose capital is neither taken nor under siege does not give in until the enemy holds this share of its home ground, by worth.
_about.assault: Storming the town, which can be tried once a month: ap is what it costs each corps that has it left, loss is how much heavier the attackers' losses are in the streets, armour is what tanks are worth there, hasty is what an assault is worth the month the army comes up to the place, by its size: a great city cannot be rushed, dice is the run of luck in the streets (a battle in the open runs from 0.8 to 1.2, and it takes 1.2 to 1 on the day to win: so an assault is an even chance at about 1.33 to 1 and sure only from 1.85), guardHit is the share of the guard a failed assault still puts out of action (percent, at even odds).
_about.breach: The works broken down, in percent of the town's bonus: by each division of besieging artillery a month (gun), by an air raid that gets through in full (raid), by a full shelling from the sea (shell); never more than most. Bombs alone break them no further than air in all (ruling 139 rider b610: the record's bombing never broke a great city's lines): a raid on works already broken that far breaks nothing more, while guns and shells still go on to most. Left alone, mend comes back each month.
_about.bombard: Softening a town from the air and the sea. raidFull is how many bombers must get through for an air raid in full, shellFull the weight of ships' guns for a shelling in full; less does its share. A bombardment in full takes org off the organisation of each corps inside (never below floor) and puts guard percent of the town guard out of action. intensity is how hard a month of raids on a town is flown beside a fight for the sky, and value is what a raid in full on one division inside counts for when the raid is judged.
_about.sortie: The share of the garrison's attacking strength that joins a relieving army's attack.
_about.pay: The share of its worth a province under siege still pays the country that holds its town.
_about.capital: How far a capital counts as lost, when its country reckons whether to ask for terms, while an army strong enough to close the ring stands round it (1 is lost outright). A government shut in loses its hold month by month: nothing in the month the ring closes, this much after capitalAfter months of siege, and after capitalYear months the capital counts as lost outright. So a capital stands a siege before its country gives in.
_about.ai: The computer: hasty is the odds it wants before it storms a town off the march, the month it comes up, assault is the odds at which it storms one it has stood round for a month, late the odds it settles for once the siege has lasted two months, last the gamble it takes when the siege has dragged on for that many months, sea what it does about a port that ships still feed and so cannot be starved (after that many months round one only the ring stays and the rest of the army goes to overrun the country behind it; blockade is how much its admirals make of closing the sea off such a port, where 5 is a fleet's usual beat and 30 the sea behind an enemy landing), relief the odds at which it attacks an army round a town of its own side (its capital, any other), relieved how it treats a town whose siege a relieving army has just raised (for that many months it comes back at the country round it only with that much better odds than it usually asks), sally the odds at which its garrison comes out against the army round it, invest how many divisions it wants outside for each one inside before it closes round a city whose defenders have all gone into it, raid how much more its air staff makes of a raid on a town its army stands round than of other bombing, hold is how many corps it puts into a threatened city or capital, as long as one is left in the field; great (ruling 139) names the great cities: every capital, and every city whose fortress works stand at that level or higher. With the enemy next door, a staff keeps the field round a great city of its own held first: while its corps there stand at 'field' times the enemy's strength next door, only the corps it can spare go inside, infantry first; where the field cannot be held, the city is filled to its room, a lone corps and all (the design director's b512(e): filling it first emptied the field and let the ring close). A garrison put in for a war that has ended comes out with the peace (b512(f)). A staff goes to the relief of any great city at a capital's odds. 'on' is false: as first built it lost Leningrad more often, not less (b509), so it waits until the mend meets its marks; TC_GREAT=1 turns it on for a measure.
